newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-REPORTER SUES NETS' COACH FOR RACIST REMARKS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-REPORTER SUES NETS' COACH FOR RACIST REMARKS.

text.p: A reporter has filed a law suit against New Jersey Nets coach John Calipari for offensive remarks made by the coach earlier this year.

Calipari, in his first season as the coach, called Dan Garcia, a Mexican-American and reporter for the Newark Star Ledger, a "(expletive deleted) Mexican idiot," after a team practice on March 20th. Calipari later apologised for the remark, but was fined $25,000 by the National Basketball Association.

Calipari was complaining to another reporter about the coverage the team receives when he spotted Garcia, a reporter for the Newark Star Ledger, and made the comment. A 10-minute, profanity-filled argument between Calipari and Garcia ensued. Shortly thereafter, the Nets issued an apology and Calipari apologised to Garcia.

Though no specific amount of damages was asked for in the suit, Kenneth McElwee, Garcia's attorney, told the Star Ledger that, "Our research has revealed verdicts in excess of $5 million in cases that are not as egregious as the facts in this case."
The suit, filed in state superior court, claims Garcia suffered "extreme humiliation and emotional distress" and seeks both compensatory and punitive damages.
Garcia has covered the Nets for the last nine years. As a reult of the lawsuit, he will be reassigned to a different beat according to Star Ledger sports editor Kevin Whitmer.
